details: No SPF record (v=spf1) found at naked.test.
exact_fixes: DNS TXT -> host: naked.test | value: v=spf1 include:YOUR_PROVIDER -all | suggested TTL: 3600
implications: An attacker can send forged email using your domain and amplify phishing campaigns.
recommendations: Publish a TXT at naked.test: "v=spf1 include:your-provider -all" (adjust includes/IPs to real ones).

details: No DKIM TXT found for selector 'default' at default._domainkey.naked.test.
exact_fixes: DNS TXT -> host: default._domainkey.naked.test | value: v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=<PUBLIC_KEY_BASE64>.
implications: An attacker can exploit the absence of effective DKIM to impersonate domain communications.
recommendations: Publish the DKIM key for 'default' at default._domainkey.naked.test in the form v=DKIM1; p=<public key>.

exact_fixes: DNS TXT -> host: _dmarc.test | suggested initial value: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@test; pct=100
implications: Receivers have no policy to block spoofing of the domain in the From field.
missing: TXT _dmarc.naked.test or inheritance from the organizational domain
recommendations: Publish DMARC starting with monitoring mode: "v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@test" and escalate with pct after inventory.

details: With only an address/domain the ARC chain cannot be validated.
exact_fixes: Export a real .eml from a forwarding flow and run it with --file to validate ARC end-to-end.
implications: You will not detect whether a malicious forwarding chain is altering or hiding authentication.
recommendations: To validate ARC you need a real .eml with ARC-Seal, ARC-Message-Signature and ARC-Authentication-Results.
